full_text_zh:
[P1] 小房子
手机淘宝扫一扫

[P2] 小房子

[美] 维吉尼亚·李·伯顿◎著绘
艾柯◎译

天津出版传媒集团
百花文艺出版社

[P3] 很久以前，
在离城市很远的乡下，
有一座小房子。
这座小房子盖得真好！
又漂亮又结实。
盖这座房子的主人说：
“小房子永远不能卖，
给多少钱都不卖。她要看着
我们的孙子的孙子的孙子的
孙子的孙子的孙子住在里面。”

[P4] 小房子坐落在山冈上，
开心地看着身边的田园风光：
清晨，她看着太阳升起，
黄昏，她看着太阳落下。
一天又一天，
每天都有点儿不一样……
可小房子总是老样子。

[P5] SUN MON TUE WED THU FRI SAT

每天晚上，
她看着月亮慢慢变化，
从一弯新月变成一轮满月；
然后，又变回一弯清瘦的月亮。
没有月光的时候，
她就看星星，
还有远方城市里的灯光。
小房子对那里很好奇，
住在城里是什么样呢？

[P6] 时间从小房子
身边悄悄溜走，
她看着田园在季节的脚步中
变换模样。
春天来了，
白天日渐加长，
阳光暖和起来，
她等待着从南方飞回的
第一只知更鸟。
她看着草地慢慢变绿，
树枝上跳出嫩绿的新芽，
她看着苹果树在风中笑开了花，
孩子们在小溪里玩耍。

[P7] 长长的夏日，
她坐在阳光下，
看着层层叠叠的树木，
为自己披上绿衣裳。
她看着白色的雏菊铺满山冈。
花园里一片欣欣向荣。
她看着苹果熟得通红，
孩子们在池塘里游泳。

[P8] 到了秋天，
白天一天天缩短，
夜晚越来越冷，
她看着第一场霜降
浸染开一片又一片绿叶。
山间闪烁着黄色、橙色和红色的叶片。
她看着人们收割庄稼、
采摘苹果。
她看着孩子们
回到学校去读书。

[P9] 不知不觉冬天来了，
夜晚更长，白天更短，
白雪覆盖着乡村田园。
她看着孩子们
溜冰、滑雪橇。
一年又一年……
苹果树老了，
地里又种上了新树。
孩子们长大了，
离开这里去了城市。
现在，每到夜里，
城市的灯光好像
越发明亮、越发靠近了。

[P10] 一天，小房子
惊讶地看到，
弯弯曲曲的乡间小路上，
开来一辆不用马拉的车……
没多久，出现了更多这样的车，
用马拉的车越来越少了。
不久，一群测量员来了，
在小房子前面测量出一条路线。
接着，又来了一辆蒸汽挖土机，
在铺满雏菊的山冈上挖开一条路……
后来，一些卡车来了，在路上卸下大石头，
卸下小石头，
卸下沥青和沙子，
最后，来了一辆蒸汽压路机，
把一切都压平——
一条公路修好了。

[P11] 现在，小房子
看着各种各样的汽车
从城市那边开过来，又开过去。
加油站……
路边店……
各种各样的小房子
沿着公路两侧盖起来。
每个人、每样东西，
都移动得比以前快多了。

[P12] 公路越来越多，
把乡村田园分割成一块一块的。
房子越来越多，
盖得又高又大。
住宅区、公寓楼、
学校、商店、修车铺……
一个接一个出现在这片土地上，
堆挤在小房子周围。
已经没有人愿意住在小房子里，
也没有人再来照顾她。
小房子永远不能卖，
所以她只能待在那儿，看着。

[P13] 现在夜里不再安宁，
城市的灯光很亮、很近，
沿途的路灯彻夜通明。
“住在城里就是这样吧。”
小房子想，
她不知道自己喜不喜欢这样。
她怀念开满雏菊的山冈，
和月光下跳舞的苹果树。

[P14] 没过多久，
有轨电车
出现在小房子门前。
整个白天和大半个晚上，
它们都开来开去。
每个人看上去都很忙碌，
每个人看上去都行色匆匆。

[P15] 没过多久，
一辆高架列车
从小房子上面呼啸而过。
空气中到处是灰尘，
噪音也非常大，
震得小房子直抖。
现在她分不清几时是春天、几时是夏天。
秋天和冬天都去哪儿了？
一切看上去总是一个样。

[P16] 没过多久，
一辆地铁
从小房子下面呼啸而过。
她虽然看不到，
却能听到，也能感觉到。
人们移动得越来越快、越来越快，
没人会注意小房子。
他们匆匆而过，来不及看她一眼。

[P17] 没过多久，
人们拆掉小房子周围的
住宅区和公寓楼，
开始挖大坑……一边一个。
蒸汽挖土机在这边挖出三层楼的深坑，
在那边挖出四层楼的深坑。
上面建起了新的大楼——
这边二十五层，
那边三十五层。

[P18] 现在，
小房子只能在中午时见到太阳，
夜晚，
再也看不到星星和月亮，
因为城市的灯光实在太亮了。
她不喜欢住在城里。
经常梦见乡下，
那开满雏菊的山冈，
和月光下跳舞的苹果树。
小房子
很孤独、也很难过。
她外面的彩色涂漆裂开了，落满灰尘，
她的窗户坏了，百叶窗斜斜地挂着。
她看上去很破旧……虽然里面还像从前一样好。

[P19] 在一个晴朗的春日早晨，
那位建造了小房子的主人的
孙子的孙子的孙女来了。
她看到这破旧的小房子，并没有匆匆而过。
仿佛小房子有种不同寻常的东西让她停下脚步。
她对丈夫说：“这个小房子像是我奶奶小时候住过的，
只是那个小房子在离城市很远的乡下，
一个铺满雏菊的山冈上，
周围长着苹果树。”

[P20] 最终他们发现，这就是那个小房子。
于是他们找到搬家公司，
问问小房子还能不能搬走。
搬家公司把小房子仔细检查了一遍，说：
“当然能。这房子和以前一样好。
她盖得很结实，我们可以把她搬到任何地方。”
于是，他们用起重机把小房子放到拖车上。
搬走她的时候交通停了几个小时，
她被慢慢拖着，离开了城市。

[P21] 一开始，小房子有点儿害怕。
可她习惯后，觉得挺好玩儿。
他们沿着大路向前滑，
他们沿着小路向前滑，
一直去到离城市很远的乡下。
当小房子看到绿草青青，
听到鸟儿鸣叫，她再也不难过了。
他们走啊走，可似乎就是找不到
特别合适的地方。
他们让小房子在这儿试试，
到那儿试试……
终于，他们看到一个小山冈，
正好在一片原野的中央，
周围长着苹果树。
“看那儿，”主人的孙子的孙子的孙女说，
“那个地方正合适。”
“是的，就是那儿。”小房子也对自己说。
他们在小山顶上挖了一个坑，
然后慢慢把小房子从路上移到山上。

[P22] 窗户和百叶窗修好了，
人们再一次给她涂上
漂亮的粉红色油漆。
当小房子在这片新地方
安顿下来时，
她高兴地笑了。
她又可以看见
太阳、月亮和星星。
她又可以看见
春天和夏天，
秋天和冬天，
轮回流转。
再一次，
有人住进了小房子，
又来照顾她了。

[P23] 她再也不会对城市好奇了，
也不想去那儿了。
天上的星星对她眨眼睛，
弯弯的月亮升上天空。
这里是春天——乡村处处平和、安宁。
full_text_en:
[P1] Little House
Scan with Taobao app

[P2] Little House

[USA] Virginia Lee Burton ◎ Author and Illustrator
Ai Ke ◎ Translator

Tianjin Publishing Media Group
Baihua Literature and Art Publishing House

[P3] Long ago,
far away from the city, in the countryside,
there was a little house.
This little house was built so well!
It was beautiful and sturdy.
The owner who built this house said:
"This little house can never be sold,
no matter how much money is offered. She wants to see
our grandson's grandson's grandson's
grandson's grandson's grandson living inside."

[P4] The little house sits on a hill,
cheerfully watching the countryside around her:
In the morning, she watches the sun rise,
in the evening, she watches the sun set.
Day after day,
every day is a little different...
but the little house always stays the same.

[P5] SUN MON TUE WED THU FRI SAT

Every evening,
she watched the moon slowly change,
from a crescent moon into a full moon;
then, back into a thin, slender moon.
When there was no moonlight,
she watched the stars,
and the lights of the distant city.
The little house was very curious about it—
what was it like to live in the city?

[P6] Time slips quietly by the little house,
She watches the fields change with the seasons.
Spring has come,
Days grow longer,
The sun warms up,
She waits for the first robin returning from the south.
She watches the grass slowly turn green,
New buds leap out from the branches,
She watches apple trees bloom in the wind,
Children play in the little stream.

[P7] Long summer days,
She sits in the sunlight,
Watching layers of trees,
Putting on her green dress.
She watches white daisies cover the hill.
The garden is full of vitality.
She watches apples ripen red,
Children swimming in the pond.

[P8] Autumn arrived,
the days grew shorter and shorter,
the nights colder and colder.
She watched the first frost
spread over leaf after leaf.
Hills shimmered with yellow, orange, and red leaves.
She watched people harvest crops,
pick apples.
She watched children
return to school to study.

[P9] Unknowingly, winter has come,
Nights grow longer, days shorter,
Snow covers the countryside.
She watches the children
Skating, sledding.
Year after year...
The apple trees grow old,
New trees are planted in the fields.
The children grow up,
Leaving here for the city.
Now, every night,
The city lights seem
Brighter and closer.

[P10] One day, the little house
was surprised to see,
on the winding country road,
a car that didn't need horses to pull it...
Soon, more of these cars appeared,
and horse-drawn vehicles became fewer and fewer.
Not long after, a group of surveyors arrived,
measuring out a route in front of the little house.
Then, a steam shovel came,
digging a path through the hillside covered with daisies...
Later, trucks arrived, unloading big rocks,
then small rocks,
then asphalt and sand.
Finally, a steam roller came,
pressing everything flat—
a road was built.

[P11] Now, the little house
watches all kinds of cars
come from the city and go back again.
Gas stations...
Roadside shops...
All kinds of little houses
are built along both sides of the road.
Everyone and everything
moves much faster than before.

[P12] More and more roads,
breaking up the countryside into pieces.
More and more houses,
built tall and big.
Residential areas, apartment buildings,
schools, shops, repair shops...
one after another appearing on this land,
crowding around the little house.
No one wanted to live in the little house anymore,
and no one came to take care of her.
The little house could never be sold,
so she could only stay there, watching.

[P13] Now the nights are no longer peaceful,
the city lights are bright and close,
and the streetlights along the way shine all night long.
"This is what living in the city must be like," thought the little house.
She didn't know if she liked it or not.
She missed the hillside covered in daisies,
and the apple tree dancing under the moonlight.

[P14] Not long after,
streetcars
appeared in front of the little house.
All day and most of the night,
they came and went.
Everyone looked busy,
everyone looked hurried.

[P15] Not long after,
An elevated train
Rushed over the little house.
The air was full of dust,
The noise was very loud,
Shaking the little house.
Now she couldn't tell when it was spring or summer.
Where had autumn and winter gone?
Everything looked the same all the time.

[P16] Not long after,
A subway train
Rushed past beneath the little house.
She couldn't see it,
But she could hear it, and feel it.
People moved faster and faster,
No one noticed the little house.
They hurried by, not even glancing at her.

[P17] Not long after,
people tore down the residential areas and apartment buildings around the little house,
and began digging big pits—one on each side.
Steam excavators dug a pit three stories deep on this side,
and a pit four stories deep on that side.
On top, new skyscrapers rose—
this one twenty-five stories high,
that one thirty-five stories high.

[P18] Now,
the little house can only see the sun at noon,
and at night,
no stars or moon are visible,
because the city lights are simply too bright.
She doesn't like living in the city.
She often dreams of the countryside,
the hillside covered with daisies,
and the apple tree dancing under the moonlight.
Little house
is very lonely and sad.
Her colorful paint is cracked and covered in dust,
her windows are broken, and her shutters hang crookedly.
She looks very old and worn... though inside, she's still as good as before.

[P19] On a bright spring morning,
the granddaughter of the grandson of the owner who built the little house arrived.
She saw the old, run-down little house and did not pass by in a hurry.
It seemed as if there was something unusual about the little house that made her stop.
She said to her husband, "This little house looks like the one my grandmother lived in when she was young,
only that little house was in the countryside, far from the city,
on a hill covered with daisies,
with apple trees growing around it."

[P20] Finally, they discovered that this was the little house.
So they found a moving company,
and asked if the little house could still be moved.
The moving company carefully inspected the house and said:
"Of course. This house is just as good as before.
It's built very solidly; we can move it anywhere."
Then, they used a crane to place the little house onto a trailer.
When they moved her, traffic stopped for several hours,
and she was slowly dragged away from the city.

[P21] At first, the little house was a bit afraid.
But after she got used to it, she found it quite fun.
They slid along the big road,
They slid along the little road,
All the way to the countryside far from the city.
When the little house saw the green grass,
And heard the birds singing, she was no longer sad.
They walked and walked, but seemed to find no
Particularly suitable place.
They let the little house try here,
And try there...
Finally, they saw a little hill,
Right in the middle of a meadow,
Surrounded by apple trees.
"Look there," said the owner's grandson's grandson's granddaughter,
"That place is just right."
"Yes, that's it," the little house said to herself.
They dug a hole on top of the hill,
And then slowly moved the little house from the road up onto the hill.

[P22] The windows and shutters were repaired,
and people painted her again with
beautiful pink paint.
When the little house settled in this new place,
she smiled happily.
She could see the sun, moon, and stars again.
She could see spring and summer,
autumn and winter,
rotating in cycles.
Once more,
someone moved into the little house,
and came to take care of her.

[P23] She would never be curious about the city again,
and didn't want to go there.
The stars in the sky blinked at her,
and the crescent moon rose into the sky.
This is spring—the countryside is peaceful and tranquil everywhere.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页展示了绘本《小房子》的封面，画面中央是一个圆形构图，描绘了一座位于绿色山丘上的小房子，周围有开花的树木和活动的人物，整体氛围宁静美好。
[P2] 本页为绘本《小房子》的扉页，展示了书名、作者、译者及出版社信息，并配有一幅小房子坐落在绿丘上的插图。
[P3] 本页讲述了很久以前，在远离城市的乡下，有一座漂亮结实的小房子，主人发誓永远不卖，希望它能传给子孙后代居住。画面描绘了小房子坐落在绿草如茵的山坡上，周围有树木、花朵和一家人在散步。
[P4] 小房子坐落在山冈上，每天看着太阳升起和落下，欣赏着田园风光，虽然周围每天都有些变化，但小房子本身始终如一。
[P5] 本页描绘了小房子在夜晚观察月亮变化和远方城市灯光的场景，表达了它对城市生活的好奇。
[P6] 本页描绘了春天到来时，小房子周围的田园景色变化，包括草地变绿、树木发芽、苹果树开花，以及孩子们在溪边玩耍的景象，展现了生机勃勃的春日田园生活。
[P7] 本页描绘了小房子在夏日里所见的田园风光，包括绿树成荫、雏菊盛开、苹果成熟和孩子们在池塘游泳的景象，展现了宁静而生机勃勃的乡村生活。
[P8] 本页描绘了秋天到来时的田园景象，小房子看着树叶变色、人们收割庄稼和采摘苹果，以及孩子们回到学校读书。
[P9] 本页描绘了冬天到来时，小房子周围的乡村被白雪覆盖，孩子们在雪地里溜冰、滑雪橇。随着时间推移，苹果树老去，孩子们长大后离开乡村去了城市，而远处城市的灯光似乎越来越明亮、越来越近。
[P10] 小房子目睹了乡间小路被改造成公路的过程，从测量、挖掘到铺设材料，最终一条新公路建成。
[P11] 小房子目睹了公路建成后，各种汽车在公路上穿梭，加油站和路边店相继出现，沿路盖起了许多新房子，整个乡村的生活节奏变得越来越快。
[P12] 本页描绘了乡村迅速城市化的景象，公路和高楼不断增多，小房子被包围在密集的建筑和车流中，无人居住也无人照料，只能孤独地见证这一切变化。
[P13] 小房子被城市灯光包围，夜晚不再安宁，它怀念过去宁静的乡村生活，如开满雏菊的山冈和月光下的苹果树。
[P14] 有轨电车出现在小房子门前，整天穿梭不息，人们行色匆匆，生活节奏变得忙碌而紧张。
[P15] 高架列车在小房子上方呼啸而过，带来灰尘和噪音，小房子被震动，它再也分不清四季，周围环境变得单调而喧嚣。
[P16] 小房子被城市交通包围，地铁在它下方呼啸而过，人们行色匆匆，无人注意它，小房子感到被忽视和孤独。
[P17] 小房子周围的住宅区和公寓楼被拆除，人们开始挖掘深坑，准备建造高层建筑，城市化进程进一步加快。
[P18] 小房子被高楼和城市灯光包围，只能在中午见到太阳，夜晚看不到星星和月亮，它感到孤独和难过，怀念乡下的宁静生活，外表破旧但内心依然完好。
[P19] 在一个晴朗的春日早晨，建造小房子的主人的曾孙女来到城市，被破旧的小房子吸引而停下脚步，她向丈夫回忆起奶奶小时候住在乡下、周围有雏菊和苹果树的温馨场景。
[P20] 小房子被发现后，搬家公司检查确认其完好无损，随后用起重机将其吊上拖车，在交通暂停数小时后，小房子被缓缓拖离了城市。
[P21] 小房子被从城市运往乡下，在途中逐渐适应并感到快乐，最终在一片长满苹果树的原野中央的小山冈上找到了新家。
[P22] 小房子被修缮并安顿在乡下的新家，重新看见了四季和星空，有人再次住进并照顾它。
[P23] 小房子在乡下的新家安顿下来，夜晚星空下，它感到平和与安宁，不再向往城市生活。
